tagline: A relaxed Asian side waterfront district with a great coastal park, weekend markets, and a more tranquil pace than neighbouring Kartal or Kadıköy.

items.name: Sahil Café Maltepe
items.description: Waterfront café along the Maltepe coastline with views of the Princes' Islands. Relaxed and unhurried — perfect for a long morning coffee.

items.name: Bağlarbaşı Kahveleri
items.description: A cluster of neighbourhood cafés around Bağlarbaşı Square. Very local crowd, good Turkish tea and coffee at honest prices.

items.name: Maltepe Sahil Restoranları
items.description: A line of seafood and traditional restaurants along the waterfront promenade. Fresh fish and mezes with Princes' Islands views.

items.name: Bağlarbaşı Lokantalari
items.description: Honest, home-style Turkish cooking in the Bağlarbaşı neighbourhood. Rotating daily menus of traditional dishes at very local prices.

items.name: Maltepe Sahil Parkı
items.description: One of Istanbul's longest and best-maintained waterfront parks. Cycling paths, green space, and beautiful Princes' Islands views on clear days.
items.tip: The park is busiest on weekend mornings with joggers and cyclists. Weekday evenings are magical and peaceful.

items.name: Weekend Flea Market
items.description: A popular weekend market along the Maltepe coast selling antiques, secondhand goods, and local produce. Great for browsing.
items.tip: Saturday mornings are the best time. Arrive before 10am for the best finds before the crowds.

items.name: Maltepe Park AVM
items.description: A well-stocked shopping centre with cinema and dining. Good for a rainy day or practical errands.

tips: Maltepe is on the M4 metro line — direct connection to Kadıköy and Sabiha Gökçen Airport.
The coastal park is one of the longest green waterfronts in Istanbul — worth cycling end to end.
Much more residential and tranquil than Kadıköy. A good base if you want Asian side living without the Kadıköy buzz.
Ferry connections to the Princes' Islands are also possible from Maltepe İskelesi.
